now_yours.text: This circle had no admin left, so running it has come to you: you can admit people, change the rules and remove someone. You did not ask for this, and nobody appointed you.
now_yours.doc: Said in the circle, to the ONE person the roster fold appointed when the last admin left. The appointment is DERIVED, so every device reaches it alone and offline — and so it happened in complete silence: nothing recorded it and the person it happened to had no way to learn it. This is the line that says it out loud. Three facts, none of them optional: the circle had no admin left; what running it now means (admit, change the rules, remove); and that nobody chose them. Shown again on a later open until they sign for it — for “a circle became yours” that is the right kind of persistence.

acknowledge.doc: The one button on the caretaker notice. Tapping it emits the caretaker’s own signed statement (the acknowledgeCaretaker op), which is what stops the notice repeating. The device must never sign on render: the whole value of the signature is that it means the person SAW it, not that a screen was drawn.

you_were_removed.text: You are no longer a member of this circle. An admin removed you. What was already here stays yours and you can keep reading it; new messages will not arrive.
you_were_removed.doc: Said in the circle, to the ONE person an admin removed, on their own device. Until 2026-08-27 this was said nowhere: the eviction was correct — signed, folded, key rotated — and their screen looked exactly as it had a second earlier, so they went on typing into a circle that could not hear them. Three facts, none optional: they are out; a person did it (not a fault or a glitch); and what they already have is not taken away, because it is theirs and a restriction there would be a costume anyway. The REASON the admin recorded is deliberately not shown — see SHOW_REMOVAL_REASON in removalNotice.js.

your_key_forked.text: Your key signed two different versions of your history in this circle. That usually means someone else has your key. From that moment you are out of this circle; what you did before stands. Replace your recovery phrase, or revoke the device you no longer have.
your_key_forked.doc: Fork notice to the person whose key forked (L133, 2026-09-25) — the one who must act. Says what happened, what it most likely means, and what to do; never accuses.

Kept written so flipping that flag is a one-line change rather than a translation task — and so the wording is decided in the calm rather than at the moment someone wants the feature. The reason was typed by one person ABOUT another and never for their eyes, and the removed member has no channel left to answer it.

1d.text: After a day, an admin can decide on their own if not enough people have voted.

7d.text: After a week, an admin can decide on their own if not enough people have voted. This keeps a decision from being stuck forever when people don't respond.

30d.text: After a month, an admin can decide on their own. Decisions can sit open for a long time.

open-ended.text: An admin can never force a decision. If not enough people vote, it stays open indefinitely — nothing is decided until the circle decides it.

off.text: No AI assistance in this circle — nothing is sent to any model.

local.text: AI runs on a member's own machine (Ollama). Messages stay on-device; nothing goes to the cloud.

cloud.text: AI runs on an independent cloud model. Your messages are sent to that provider when you ask it something.

yes.text: Anyone can add an AI agent as a participant. Agents can read whatever the circle shares.

admin-approval.text: AI agents may join only after an admin approves — a checkpoint before any agent sees circle content.

no.text: No AI agents may join. Only people take part in this circle.

pairwise.text: Real names are revealed one-to-one. Each member chooses who gets to see their identity.

open.text: Every member can see each other's real names. There is no per-person hiding.

none.text: Nothing is stored to a pod. Data lives only on members' devices and is lost if they clear it.

shared.text: One shared pod holds the circle's data — every member reads and writes the same store.

personal.text: Each member keeps their own pod and the circle links to them by reference. You keep control of your own copy.

hybrid.text: A shared pod plus personal pods: common items are shared, private items stay with each member.

closed.text: Items can't be shared outside this circle. Sharing out is turned off.

copy.text: Sharing out sends a separate, freshly sealed copy to the recipient. They get their own copy — later edits in the circle don't reach it, and you can't take it back.

trusted.text: The live item itself is shared in place: the recipient is given a key to open the circle's own copy, no duplicate is made. Any member can share an item this way.

registered.text: Same live, in-place sharing as 'Live share (members)', but only an admin may add a recipient. Members can't share items out on their own.

canonical.text: The item stays in place in this circle — no copy is made. The recipient gets a revocable key to open it. Un-sharing rotates the key so they lose access.

admin_only.text: Only an admin of this circle can do this.
admin_only.doc: A ⋯ menu entry reserved for the circle's admins, shown greyed to a member with this sentence beside it (invite keeps its own, more specific one). Names the role, never the people who hold it.

not_in_this_circle.text: That is not something this circle does — the app it belongs to is not switched on here. An admin can turn it on in the settings.
not_in_this_circle.doc: Said when a person invokes an op whose APP this circle does not compose. It used to answer "I couldn't turn that into an action", which blames the person for the circle's configuration. Names what is wrong AND who can change it, because a refusal a person cannot act on is only slightly better than silence.

feature_off.text: That is switched off in this circle. An admin can turn it on.
feature_off.doc: Said when the op exists here but its FEATURE is off (the circle's `requires` gate). Distinct from not_in_this_circle: the app is present, the circle has chosen not to use this part of it.

not_yours.text: That is not something you can do here.
not_yours.doc: Said when the capability matrix refuses this member. Deliberately short and not apologetic: it is a statement about what this circle grants, not about the person. It does NOT say who could do it — that would name people to somebody who has just been refused.

connected.doc: The contact's PAIR ROSTER exists (L105): a hidden two-member circle made on the first exchange, so messages travel over a roster and a revoke reaches them. Before it exists: no label (Frits: no 'kaart').

hide.doc: L106 (Frits 2026-09-19): hide a contact from Contacten — the row stays (thread, pair roster, their circles untouched), it folds away at the bottom, and their next message brings them back. On every device of the person. The thread header's control when the contact is shown.

unhide.doc: The thread header's control when the contact is hidden: show them in Contacts again (the person's own act; a message from them does the same).

hide_note.text: Only from your list. Their circles and this conversation stay; a message from them brings them back.
hide_note.doc: What hiding IS and is not, said under the control (amendment 3: Contacts only — their circles, roster row and member card are untouched). Never a notification.

hidden_fold.doc: The fold at the bottom of Contacts holding the hidden rows; tapping it shows them (greyed). count = how many.

returned_marker.doc: The one-line marker painted in the thread when a hidden contact writes again and comes back — so the person understands why someone they removed is in their list. Wilfred (the seeded contact) never initiates, so for him it is only ever a reply.

returned_deleted_marker.text: You had deleted this contact. They wrote again, so they are back.

delete.doc: Thread header — delete this contact (L114): hide + leave the pair circle. Opens a confirm sheet first.

delete_title.doc: Confirm sheet heading for deleting a contact (L114).

delete_body.text: {{name}} disappears from your contacts on all your devices and your shared connection closes. Your conversation stays on this device. If {{name}} writes to you again, they come back.

The op is `setMemberRole`; the roster fold on every device is what actually decides, so this is a convenience, not the gate.

demote.text: {{name}} will no longer run this circle. The other admins keep it.

handover.text: {{name}} is the only admin. After this nobody is running this circle, so it passes to one of the other members — which one follows from the log; nobody picks.
handover.doc: Confirm body when the LAST admin steps back. The fold answers this by handing over (appointing a caretaker from whoever is left), not by refusing it, so the person must be told that the circle changes hands. Deliberately does NOT name the successor: that is derived from the log and a shell guessing at it would give one circle two stories.

no_one_else.text: {{name}} is the only admin and there is nobody else in this circle to take over, so this cannot take effect: {{name}} stays admin.
no_one_else.doc: Confirm body when the last admin is also the only member. There is nobody to hand to, so the fold keeps the demotion from standing at all — said plainly here instead of a handover that cannot happen.

promoted.text: {{name}} is now an admin of this circle.

demoted.text: {{name}} is no longer an admin of this circle.
demoted.doc: Panel notice after an ordinary demotion.

handed_over.text: {{name}} is no longer an admin. The circle has passed to one of the other members.
handed_over.doc: Panel notice after the last admin stepped back — the same handover the confirm announced, restated as what happened. Names no successor: the member list shows who, once the roster reloads.

no_one_else.text: {{name}} is still an admin: there is nobody else in this circle to take over.
no_one_else.doc: Panel notice when the demotion could not stand — the circle would have been left with nobody to run it.

restore_finish.status_ready: You are you again, and your circles are here.
restore_finish.empty_title: You are you again. Your circles are not here.
restore_finish.empty_body: The phrase brings back who you are, not the list of circles you were in. That list lives on your pod, or in a recovery file you saved. If you have neither, someone in each circle can invite you again; you come back as the same member.
restore_finish.later_title: Fine. You can load a file later under My data.
restore_finish.intent_question: Could anyone else still use your old phone?
restore_finish.intent_broken: No, it broke or I wiped it
restore_finish.intent_lost: Maybe, it is lost or stolen
restore_finish.intent_adding: It still works, I am adding this one
restore_finish.intent_hint: Broken or lost, the app does the same thing: your old phone stops counting as you. The difference is only what we tell you.
restore_finish.phrase_body: Type your recovery phrase once more to finish.
restore_finish.done_quiet: Done. This is your phone now.
restore_finish.done_loud: Done. Your old phone can no longer act as you in any circle. Whatever it already read stays read; nothing new reaches it.
restore_finish.err_not_yours: That file was not made with your recovery phrase.
restore_finish.err_unreadable: That is not a recovery file.
restore_finish.err_failed: That did not work. You can try again under My data.

replace.title: This is my phone now
replace.body: Type the recovery phrase. Every other device of yours is retired in all your circles, and what they could read comes along to this one. Use this after a phone broke or went missing.
replace.done: Done. Your other devices are retired everywhere; this one carries on.

revoke.title: Remove a device
revoke.body: Type the recovery phrase to remove this device everywhere. Its keys stop being accepted in all your circles; the device itself becomes an island.
revoke.done: Device removed. Every circle now refuses its keys.

companionClaim.title: Claim a companion
companionClaim.body: Paste the line your companion shows in its log, after 'Claim:' (code@address). It becomes yours: every device of yours can manage it, a revoked device cannot.
companionClaim.done: This companion is yours now. Every device of yours can manage it.
companionClaim.outcome_bad_claim: That is not a claim line. Copy everything after 'Claim:' — the code, the @ and the address.
companionClaim.outcome_no_device_key: This device has no device key of its own yet. Open the app again and try once more.
companionClaim.outcome_unreachable: The companion does not answer. Is it running and connected to the relay?
companionClaim.outcome_already_owned: This companion already has an owner.
companionClaim.outcome_invalid_code: The code is wrong or has expired. Take the newest line from the log (a new one every ten minutes).
companionClaim.outcome_stale: This device's clock is more than five minutes off the companion's. Set your device's time right and try again.
companionClaim.outcome_unsigned: The companion did not accept this device's signature.

companionGrant.to_none: Nobody to give access to yet. First add the bot as a contact (its card), or link it with /koppel.
companionGrant.loading: Asking what this companion can give…
companionGrant.done: Access given. The companion passes it on; it holds until you revoke it (tick it again after a year).
companionGrant.outcome_not_owned: This companion is not yours. Claim it first.
companionGrant.outcome_no_device_key: This device has no device key of its own yet. Reopen the app and try again.
companionGrant.outcome_unreachable: The companion does not answer. Is it on and connected to the relay?
companionGrant.outcome_forbidden: The companion did not accept this device's signature.
companionGrant.outcome_stale: This device's clock is more than five minutes off from the companion's. Set your device's time and try again.
companionGrant.outcome_bad_target: The companion cannot give access to that recipient.
companionGrant.outcome_bad_args: Choose to whom, and tick what it may do.
companionGrant.outcome_gate_off: This companion runs without its access check, so it gives no access.
companionGrant.outcome_not_bot_admin: Only the bot's admin can give it your companion. Ask them to grant it from their app.
companionGrant.outcome_bot_unreachable: The bot does not answer. Is it running and connected to the relay?
companionGrant.outcome_bot_refused: The bot did not take your companion. Link your Basis app to it again (/koppel) and try once more.
companionGrant.revoked: Revoked. The companion refuses whatever it tries here from now on.

opened_added.doc: After opening someone's contact link: the contact was added; name = their display name, handle or key.

share.doc: Mobile's one button on the share panel: the phone's share sheet with the link (or the code when the app has no web URL).

pending.doc: In the /circles summary: circles made since the app started, not active until a reload.

connectScreen.title: Connect a screen
connectScreen.label: browser
connectScreen.own_browser: Open this in your own browser (Chrome, Firefox, Safari), not in Telegram's window: the screen remembers nothing there. This screen's key stays in this browser.
connectScreen.code: 2. The bot then asks which code this screen shows. Tap this one in your chat with the bot:
connectScreen.waiting: This screen waits. Once you tapped the code, this page becomes your management screen.
connectScreen.connected: Connected to {{bot}}. This is your management screen: bookmark this page to come back to it. This screen can do this for you:
connectScreen.not_a_link: This link is not (or no longer) valid. Ask the bot for a new one: /scherm.
connectScreen.refused: Not connected: another code, or "none of these", was picked in your chat with the bot. Ask for a new link: /scherm.
connectScreen.timed_out: Not connected: no answer came within ten minutes. Ask for a new link: /scherm.
connectScreen.launch_refused: Not connected: the bot does not know you yet, or this opening was too old. Open the screen again with the button under /scherm.
connectScreen.paste_this: 1. Copy this line (the button below) and send it in your own chat with the bot:
connectScreen.stepup_expired: Not done: no yes came within ten minutes.
connectScreen.stepup_replaced: Not done: a newer request took its place.
connectScreen.stepup_failed: That did not work; see your chat.
connectScreen.stepup_unanswered: No answer: no yes came within ten minutes. Nothing changed.
connectScreen.rate_limited: Slow down a little: this screen asked too much at once. Try again in a few seconds.
connectScreen.revoked: This screen no longer works: it was connected again somewhere else, or disconnected. Open it again with /scherm in your chat with the bot.
connectScreen.elsewhere: This screen is open in another window. Carry on there, or take it back here.

identityLink.code: The bot then asks which code your app shows. Pick this one:
identityLink.no_device_key: This device cannot make a link line yet (it has no device key of its own). Open the app again and try once more.
identityLink.paste_link: Paste the link the bot sent you (it starts with https:// and contains #koppel-bot=).
identityLink.not_a_link: That is not a link from a bot's /koppel.
identityLink.linked: Linked to {{bot}}. In the chat, /ontkoppel undoes it.

leave_confirm.text: Leaving your circle can't be undone. Re-run with --confirm=true to proceed.
leave_confirm.doc: /leave-group without the confirm flag: nothing happened yet.

left.text: 👋 Left the circle. What is on this device stays; you no longer receive updates from the circle.

single_mode.doc: The mode field of the /groups record: this device works with one circle.

current_note.text: More than one circle at a time is not possible here yet.

ambiguous.text:
More than one match for '{{match}}'. Reply with the start of the id:
{{options}}
ambiguous.doc: /done, /remove, /grab or a reassign whose words fit several open items; {{options}} lists them, one per line.

not_found_task.text: Couldn't find an open task matching '{{match}}'.
not_found_task.doc: /grab or a reassign whose words fit no open task.

not_found_item.text: Couldn't find an open item matching '{{match}}'.
not_found_item.doc: /done or /remove whose words fit no open item.

reassigned.doc: Confirmation of a reassign; {{who}} is who has it now.

added_to.doc: Confirmation of /add; {{list}} is the kind of item (shopping, errand, …).

date_locale.doc: Not words: the date language (a BCP 47 tag) the days and times in this language's replies are written in — "vr 9 okt" / "Fri 9 Oct".

chore_claimed.doc: A chore was taken by the person who asked (or given to themselves). Said so that it reads right for everyone who sees it. {{when}}: the chore's day as ", vr 9 okt", or empty.

chore_theirs.doc: A chore was given to someone, by the name the person used (only where names may be seen). {{when}}: the chore's day as ", vr 9 okt", or empty.

chore_given.doc: A chore was given to someone whose name this person may not see. {{when}}: the chore's day as ", vr 9 okt", or empty.

chore_open.doc: A chore was taken away from whoever held it, and given to no one.

chore_due.doc: A chore with a day and nobody holding it yet: its day.

chore_edited.doc: A chore was changed; its words as they are now.

who_held.doc: Who does a chore ("wie doet de lamp"): the one chore the words fit, who holds it and its day. {{who}}: the holders as the reader may see them ("jou", a name, "iemand"); {{when}}: ", za 10 okt" or empty.

who_open.doc: Who does a chore: the one chore the words fit, and nobody holds it. {{when}}: ", za 10 okt" or empty.

who_none.text: There is no open chore with '{{text}}'.
who_none.doc: Who does a chore: no open chore holds the words the person used.

who_several.doc: Who does a chore: several open chores hold the words; {{chores}} is one row each (who_row_held / who_row_open), joined by "; ".

who_row_held.doc: One chore in the several-chores line: its words, who holds it and its day (", za 10 okt" or empty).

who_row_open.doc: One chore in the several-chores line that nobody holds; its day as ", za 10 okt" or empty.

who_you.doc: The reader themselves among the people of a chore or an appointment ("is van jou").

who_someone.doc: A person the reader may not name (the household's names setting): never their id.

who_everyone.doc: An appointment that names nobody: it is for the whole household.

who_nobody.doc: A chore on a day that nobody holds yet.

mine_list.doc: Someone else's open chores ("wat moet Bob doen"), by the name asked. {{chores}}: one row each (mine_row / mine_row_due), joined by "; ".

mine_none.doc: Someone else's open chores: they hold none.

mine_row.doc: One chore in someone's chores line, without a day.

mine_row_due.doc: One chore in someone's chores line, with its day ("za 10 okt").

day_head.doc: One day's read ("wie is er zaterdag"): its first line, the day as "za 10 okt".

day_event.doc: One appointment that day: its time, its title and who comes ("iedereen" when it names nobody).

day_chore.doc: One chore due that day and who does it ("nog niemand" when nobody holds it).

day_none.doc: One day's read: no appointments and no chores that day.
